bio.en: Elena Verna is a world-leading growth and monetization expert who has scaled product-led growth and product-led sales at companies including Amplitude, Miro, SurveyMonkey, MongoDB, and Netlify, and teaches experimentation and growth at Reforge.
bio.zh: Elena Verna 是世界领先的增长与变现专家，曾在 Amplitude、Miro、SurveyMonkey、MongoDB、Netlify 等公司规模化地打造产品驱动增长与产品驱动销售，并在 Reforge 教授实验与增长课程。

summary.en: Elena Verna gives a deep, opinionated masterclass on product-led sales (PLS) — the emerging go-to-market motion that turns self-serve usage into larger sales-led contracts. She distinguishes PLG (individual, self-serve monetization capped around $10K) from PLS, which builds a "bridge" from an individual user's job-to-be-done up to an enterprise-level solution, with sales owning the escalator because products are bad at conveying enterprise value. Key concepts covered: PQA (product-qualified account) vs PQL vs MQL and the three lead-attribution channels; why every sales-led company should add a product-assist element and make product accountable for pipeline; the four roles needed (product, analytics, marketing, sales) and a "Wizard of Oz" start before buying tooling; behavioral signals like admin switches and terms-of-use page views; and common pitfalls (treating PLS like top-down sales, spamming users, excluding marketing). She stresses patience (12+ months of usage before enterprise contracts) and ends by speculating that AI will automate sales conversations next.
summary.zh: Elena Verna 给了一堂有观点、极深入的产品驱动销售（PLS）大师课——这是一种新兴的 go-to-market 打法，把自助用量转化成更大的、销售驱动的合同。她区分了 PLG（个人的、自助变现上限约 1 万美元）和 PLS：PLS 在个人的"待完成任务"和企业级方案之间建一座"桥"，由销售拥有那部扶梯，因为产品不擅长传达企业价值。涵盖的关键概念：PQA（产品合格账户）vs PQL vs MQL，以及三种线索归因渠道；为什么每个销售驱动公司都该加"产品辅助"元素、并让产品对管道可问责；需要的四个角色（产品、分析、营销、销售）以及买工具前"绿野仙踪式"的起步；管理员切换、使用条款页浏览等行为信号；以及常见坑（把 PLS 当自上而下销售、spam 用户、排除营销）。她强调耐心（企业合同前需 12 个月以上用量），最后猜想下一步 AI 会自动化销售对话。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: The most important thing in product-led sales is that there is a different configuration internally of collaboration that needs to occur. In traditional sales world, marketing creates pipeline for sales. Sales sells product. Product engages with a paid user to drive retention. In the product-led sales, product acquires and activates a customer and product creates pipeline for sales, so relationship is not that there's a go-to-market org with marketing and sales and product just kind of throws features across the fence for them to sell. (00:00:40): The collaboration here is between product and sales, but that means the product has to take on accountability over pipeline. The worst thing that you can do is to say, "I'm going to do product-led growth," or, "I'm going to do product-led sales and I'm going to do it in marketing." Recipe for disaster. You'll be failure mode within six months because product has to take accountability over selling of the product itself.
turns.zh: 在产品驱动销售（product-led sales）里，最重要的是：内部需要一种不同的协作配置。传统销售世界里，营销为销售创造管道，销售卖产品，产品跟付费用户互动来驱动留存。而在产品驱动销售里，产品负责获取并激活客户、还替销售创造管道——所以关系不是"有个 go-to-market 组织，营销和销售在那，产品只是把功能扔过墙让他们去卖"。（00:00:40）这里的协作是产品与销售之间，但这意味着产品方必须承担起"管道"的责任。你能做的最糟的事就是："我要做产品驱动增长"或"我要做产品驱动销售，而且我要放在营销里做。"那是灾难配方。半年内就会失败，因为产品必须对自己产品的销售负责。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Great question, so let's start with product-led growth. We've talked about it a little bit in our first episode, but let's revisit the topic. Product led growth is all about product's ability to self-serve activate, self-serve engage, and convert that usage to a monetization opportunity. You bring people, you get them to an aha moment into the habit loops, and then you able to extract value back out of them. Extraction of the value can be direct where you're actually capturing revenue from them, or it can be indirect where they're participating in your growth model via virality or user-generated content and bring additional business through the doors. (00:08:34): Let's talk about direct phase to capture that value. There's self-serve monetization, so I'm using product self-serve. I go to the pricing page. I find the plan that best suits me on features that I want to unlock or usage that I want to unlock and I buy it. However, that's not the only way to monetize that usage. You can monetize that usage with sales, too. Why? Self-serve monetization has a cap of about $10,000. That's just how much we're able to process on the credit cards before they start getting flagged and declined by the banks and how much we as a consumers and prosumers are even willing to put on our credit card because not all credit cards have limits of over 10, 20, 30, $40,000. (00:09:15): Self-serve monetization is very much a prosumer use case where an individual is trying to solve the problem on their own. Product-led sales converts the usage that you've generated via self-serve into a sales opportunity and it attaches a salesperson to close a much larger contract, which can be 15, 20, a hundred thousand dollars in order to bring an enterprise-level solution to a company that has already been using it in a self-serve manner.
turns.zh: 好问题，先从产品驱动增长（PLG）说起。我们第一季聊过一点，再回顾下。PLG 全是关于产品"自助激活、自助参与、并把使用转化为变现机会"的能力。你带人进来，让他们到达 aha 时刻、进入习惯循环，然后从中提取价值。价值提取可以是直接的——你直接从他们身上拿到收入；也可以是间接的——他们通过病毒传播或用户生成内容参与你的增长模型，带更多生意进门。（00:08:34）聊直接变现那阶段。有自助变现：我用产品自助，去定价页，找到最符合我想解锁的功能或用量的套餐，买下。但这不是变现用量的唯一方式。你也可以用销售来变现。为什么？自助变现上限大约 1 万美元——信用卡在被银行标记、拒付之前，我们大概只能处理这个数；而且作为消费者和 prosumer，我们愿意刷在卡上的也就这么多，因为不是所有卡都有 1、2、3、4 万美元的额度。（00:09:15）自助变现非常是 prosumer 用例——一个人想自己解决问题。产品驱动销售把你通过自助产生的用量，转化成销售机会，并配上销售去签一个更大的合同——可能是 1.5 万、2 万、10 万美元——把一个已经自助使用产品的公司，带到企业级方案。

Product-led sales assumes that there's a migration from an individual use case that you acquired an end user with and an escalation into an enterprise-level solution that solves enterprise-level problems. Let me break it down and let me use just, for example, Amplitude as an example.
turns.zh: ……一个人有问题、有要完成的任务，进产品里解决它。对很多 B2B 公司，这就是 PLG 的精髓。但如果你要配一个销售，公司里没人会为"一个人解决他的问题"付 1 万、1.5 万、2 万美元。产品驱动销售假设：你用终端用户获取的"个人用例"，会升级到解决企业级问题的"企业级方案"。我拆开讲，用 Amplitude 当例子。

turns.speaker: Lenny

What is the company-level solution? Well, it's more self-serve ability of the data. It's democratization of data. It's enhanced insights in the more data-driven culture. That's what company's solving for. Individual is not solving for data-driven culture. Individual is just solving for data insights for them. Company's solving for data-driven culture. (00:11:25): In product-led growth, you can just have an individual be very happy with their solution for their job to be done. However, what product-led sales assumes is that there is an escalator to an enterprise-level solution, and enterprise escalator is valuable to attach sales resources to because products fundamentally do a really bad job at communicating enterprise-level value prop. They're very good at showing you as a user what you can do. They've very terrible at showing what organization actually can benefit out of the solution. (00:12:02): Sales can tell that story. Sales can bridge that gap, and then you can increase the perceived value in order to bridge the gap to that $15,000, 20, hundred-thousand dollar contract. I would say self-serve monetization is very much an individual use case versus product-led sales is turning that individual use case and self-serve usage into a sales pipeline with enterprise-level value.
turns.zh: Amplitude，个人想要什么？我要随手可得的数据，为我的产品做更好的决策，所以我把 Amplitude SDK 嵌进我的产品，它给我行为数据，帮我更好地建产品。公司级方案是什么？是数据的更强自助能力、是数据民主化、是更深入的洞察和更数据驱动的文化。这才是公司在解的。个人不是在解"数据驱动文化"，个人只是解"他自己的数据洞察"。公司在解"数据驱动文化"。（00:11:25）在 PLG 里，个人对他的"任务"很满意就行。但产品驱动销售假设的是：存在一个通往企业级方案的"自动扶梯"，而企业扶梯值得配销售资源，因为产品在传达企业级价值主张上做得实在很差。它们很擅长向你展示"作为用户你能做什么"，却极不擅长展示"组织究竟能从方案里得到什么好处"。（00:12:02）销售能讲这个故事，能补上这个 gap，于是你能抬高感知价值，去够那个 1.5 万、2 万、10 万美元的合同。我会说：自助变现很是个"个人用例"，而产品驱动销售是把那个个人用例和自助用量，转成带企业级价值的销售管道。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I really like that way of thinking about it. Basically product-led growth has a ceiling. You're only going to get-
turns.zh: 我真的很喜欢这个思路。本质上 PLG 有个天花板。你最多只能——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... so high in terms of spend. You can only explain things so much to a potential user and then sales comes in and solves a lot of those problems, and product-led sales is essentially this. I think you even have this visualization now that I'm thinking about-
turns.zh: ……在支出上到这么高。你能向潜在用户解释的也就这么多，然后销售进来解掉很多问题。产品驱动销售本质上就是这个。我想你现在甚至有个可视化——我正想到——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: It's a bridge.
turns.zh: 它是一座桥。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... as a bridge. Right, yeah, this bridge between the two, and so in this world of product-led sales, does sales as a function, outbound sales, continue to exist? One, and then two, is it radically different in this world of product-led sales?
turns.zh: ……一座桥。对，是两者之间那座桥。那么在这个产品驱动销售的世界里，销售这个职能、外呼销售，还会继续存在吗？第一；第二，在这个世界里它是否彻底不同了？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yeah, so to understand how sales should be applied in the situation, you need to understand end user's motivation, ability, and permission. Simple organization, so for example, if the end user is very motivated, they have full sense of ability to solve the problem and they have all of the permission from organization, or maybe not even permission, maybe forgiveness from organization, to go and explore and bring in a new solution. Then, it can be a very much organic motion up that escalator. However, that's not always the case. A lot of times the end users miss permission of solving enterprise-level problems. There's lots of stakeholders, there's a committee that has to make a decision. It impacts departments outside of their purview and maybe they even lack ability to do it. Maybe they can do their little job to be done, but not the entire enterprise-level integration. (00:13:55): In my Amplitude example, yeah, I can drop an SDK in my product area, but how do I convince entire product to adopt Amplitude and put an SDK on every single interaction across the entire app? There is different level problem statements, and this is where product-led sales is either can be a truly organic motion where people raise their hands, they submit sales forms and there's already a need, a desire, an understanding of it, or end user might hit friction points. Product-led sales has to bridge those friction points by either attracting the right decision-makers to the process so they can find an enterprise buyer out there. They can understand who's the champion and what their capabilities and what their permission levels are. They can create a committee for the decision. (00:14:46): There is... They almost slap a bandaid on the problem of people not be able to and not wanting to necessarily resolve the problem on their own. They can be very powerful with that as well as marketing because we cannot forget about marketing where they can educate of how to help people bridge that gap and how to sell things internally.
turns.zh: 对，要理解销售该怎么用，你得理解终端用户的"动机、能力、许可"。简单说，比如终端用户动机很强、完全有能力解决问题、而且有组织的许可（甚至不是许可，也许是组织的"宽恕"）去探索、引入新方案。那它可以是顺着扶梯很有机地上去。但情况不总是这样。很多时候终端用户缺的是"解决企业级问题"的许可。有好多干系人、有个委员会要做决定，它影响到他们职责范围外的部门，也许他们甚至缺乏能力——可能能完成自己的小任务，但做不了整个企业级集成。（00:13:55）拿我 Amplitude 的例子：是，我能在我的产品区域里嵌个 SDK，但怎么说服整个产品团队采纳 Amplitude、在整支 app 的每个交互上都放 SDK？那是不同层级的问题陈述。这时产品驱动销售，可以是真正有机的——人们举手、提交销售表单、需求已经在那；也可以是终端用户撞到摩擦点。产品驱动销售得补上这些摩擦点：要么把对的决策者吸引进流程，好找到企业买家；要么弄清谁是 champion、能力和许可层级如何；要么去组一个决策委员会。（00:14:46）它几乎像给"人既没能力、也不一定想自己解决"的问题贴了块创可贴。配合营销它也能很强大——别忘了营销，营销能教育人怎么补 gap、怎么在内部卖东西。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You mentioned this idea of enterprise-level problems. It might help if you give an example or two of what those might be. Then, also, just what are examples of companies that are doing enterprise or product-led sales well just to kind of give people a mental model as you're talking about some of this stuff?
turns.zh: 你提到"企业级问题"这概念。给一两个例子也许有帮助。还有，哪些公司在做企业级或产品驱动销售做得好，给点心智模型？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Sure, so let's go through a couple of them. Let's go through Miro. Miro is an online whiteboarding platform. What is individual problem that people come to Miro to solve? They have a workshop they need to facilitate. Maybe they need a board to just do brainwriting in and they use Miro for individual jobs to be done. However, what Miro is designed for is a team-level problem. I come in and I bring you in and we collaborate together, so now there's two, three, four people involved, but even that is still on the project level, it's on the team level. Nobody's going to pay a hundred thousand dollars to solve a team-level small problem that is solving. What is the enterprise-level problem? It's increased innovation, it's increased productivity across the entire team because now we have this new outlet in which we can collaborate. (00:16:10): Now, can Miro very clearly show increase in productivity across the organization by using the product? No. Can sales tell the story? Yes. Miro takes you from an individual user to a team step, and then sales bridges the gap to an enterprise. Let's give another example of Figma. In Figma, I come in as a designer and I just need a better way to capture feedback from my stakeholders, a more scalable way to capture it so I can iterate on the perfect design. What is it at the team level? Now there is a team that can collaborate with me more openly. I can capture more feedback from more stakeholders faster and get the project done sooner. (00:16:53): What is it on the enterprise level? Well, on enterprise level, our designs are just better fit the business needs. They have faster turnaround time and our product is performing better. That's an enterprise-level value prop and, again, we're, I think, in the product development space gotten a little bit lazy of actually showcasing that enterprise value in product. We rely on excellence of sales team to tell that story. I do hope that changes, by the way, in the future, that we put more pressure on the products to take it all the way up the escalator so we don't have to be a hundred percent dependent on the sales team going and showcasing that story. The product can really empower that escalator from the starting point till the end on its own.
turns.zh: 当然，过几个。先说 Miro。Miro 是在线白板平台。个人来找 Miro 解什么？他们有个工作坊要带，也许就需要一块板做 brainwriting，于是用 Miro 解个人任务。但 Miro 设计的是"团队级问题"。我进来拉你进来一起协作，于是有两、三、四个人参与，但那仍在项目层、团队层。没人会为解一个小团队问题付 10 万美元。企业级问题是什么？是创新增加、是整个团队生产力提升，因为有了这个新协作出口。（00:16:10）现在，Miro 能清晰展示"用产品让全组织生产力提升"吗？不能。销售能讲这个故事吗？能。Miro 把你从个人用户带到团队这步，然后销售补上到企业的 gap。再给个 Figma 的例子。在 Figma 里，我作为设计师进来，只想更好、更可规模化地收集干系人反馈，好迭代出完美的设计。团队层是什么？现在有个团队能更开放地跟我协作，我能更快从更多干系人收反馈、更早完成项目。（00:16:53）企业级是什么？我们的设计更贴合业务需求、周转更快、产品表现更好。那是企业级价值主张。再说一次，我觉得做产品的在空间里有点懒，没真的在产品里秀出那企业价值，我们靠销售团队的卓越去讲那故事。我真心希望未来这会改变——我们给产品更多压力，让它自己把扶梯一路顶到顶，这样就不必 100% 依赖销售团队去讲那故事。产品完全能从起点到终点自己赋能那部扶梯。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I want to dig into that for sure. I know that's something you just shared on LinkedIn recently and I thought that was a really interesting topic, but before we get there, let's talk about this bridge a little bit more. People might be listening to this that are maybe a product-led growth company and they may feel like, "Hey, wait, we're already doing this. We have this product-led growth motion, we have a sales team. They figure out who to talk to." What exactly is in that bridge that makes product-led sales so interesting? I imagine it's like helping you identify who to go after, helping people go further and further and escalate it themselves. How do you think about that bridge between product and sales?
turns.zh: 这个我肯定要深挖。我知道你刚在 LinkedIn 分享过，我觉得那话题很有意思。但在那之前，再多聊下这座桥。听众里也许有做 PLG 的公司，会觉得"嘿等等，我们已经在做这个了——我们有 PLG 打法、有销售团队，他们找出该跟谁谈。"那座桥里到底是什么，让产品驱动销售这么有意思？我猜是帮你识别该追谁、帮人自己一路升级。你怎么看产品与销售之间的桥？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Let's talk about how product-led growth companies start with product-led sales. It usually starts by an organic demand from a user base. They reach out to them through support channels by just pinging people who work at the company saying, "Hey, I want to purchase this for my entire company." That's an organic pool that you start feeling from product-led growth model into enterprise sales world and, by the way, you should never hire any salespeople until you feel that pool because if nobody's asking to purchase, then you cannot just hire an SDR and make a purchase happen. You need to see those hand-raisers, you need to see those people demanding an enterprise-level adoption. Then, you hire starts hiring salespeople to actually suffice that demand and that's great, and you're starting to do sales and surfacing really addressing organic demand within your product. (00:19:11): That organic demand very quickly dries up if you rely on hand-raisers of your champions. If you rely on having enterprise buyers in your user base that are asking to just sign on the dotted line, then you have a very limited ceiling for your growth because what majority of the usage transforms to be is to have product qualification that there's a meaningful sales conversation that could occur based on the signals within usage that the buyer is missing. 90% of product-led sales is converting the usage into an opportunity by finding a buyer outside, by finding the decision-maker outside. This is where marketing and sales are so crucial in the process. Connecting that decision-maker to the usage and then driving an opportunity through sales funnel all the way to closed one deal. (00:20:08): It's great when you start having sales team and you're surfacing this organic demand. That's beautiful and power to you. Just it doesn't last very long just because end user fundamentally does not equal enterprise buyer and that organic demand ends up plateauing very shortly because you cannot just make enterprise buyers happen from your users.
turns.zh: 我们聊聊 PLG 公司怎么开始做产品驱动销售。通常从一个用户群的有机需求起。他们通过支持渠道联系，直接 ping 公司里的人说"嘿，我想给整个公司买。"那是你从 PLG 模型感受到、流向企业销售世界的有机池子——顺便，在那池子出现前你绝不该招任何销售，因为没人主动要买，你就招个 SDR 也造不出购买。你得看到那些"举手的人"、那些要求企业级采纳的人，然后才开始招销售去满足那需求——这很好，你开始做销售、浮现并真正对接产品内的有机需求。（00:19:11）但那有机需求，若你只靠 champion 举手，很快会干涸。若你只靠用户群里的企业买家来签合同，增长天花板就很有限，因为绝大多数用量变成的是：需要有"产品资格判定"——基于买家缺失的使用信号，去判断一次有意义的销售对话是否可能发生。产品驱动销售的 90% 是：通过在外部找买家、找决策者，把用量转化成机会。这就是营销和销售在流程里如此关键的原因——把那个决策者和用量连起来，然后一路把机会推过销售漏斗，直到关单。（00:20:08）起步时有销售团队、浮现有机需求，很棒，给你点赞。只是它撑不了多久，因为终端用户 fundamentally 不等于企业买家，那有机需求很快会触顶——你没法从用户里硬造出企业买家。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: If a founder is listening to this right now and they're like, "Okay, so I have maybe a product-led growth component, they're self-serve, maybe I have a sales team, maybe I don't," what's a sign that your product is a fit for investing in product-led sales? Essentially every product-led growth-oriented company should be eventually investing in this area. Or is there certain companies that are like, "No, you don't need to worry about it, just stay product-led growth forever or just stay sales-led growth forever?"
turns.zh: 如果有个创始人现在听着，想"好，我有也许是 PLG 的部分，他们自助，也许我有销售团队、也许没有"，什么信号说明你的产品适合投入产品驱动销售？本质上每个偏 PLG 的公司最终都该投这块？还是某些公司"不，你不用管，永远做 PLG 或永远做销售驱动增长"？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: To have product-led sales means you're going upmarket-
turns.zh: 做产品驱动销售意味着你在上探市场（upmarket）——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Mm-hmm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... period. That means you going for contract values that are probably over your sales floor, so the minimum that the sales is willing to engage and close, which is traditionally around $15,000. If you're going for contract values of $15,000, that means you're probably trying to close a hundred, $200,000 contracts as well. Who can handle a hundred, $200,000 contract? It's not going to be a small startup. It's not going to be an SMB. It's probably going to be higher end of more of a mid-market segment, so 200 employees-plus. More likely it's going to be towards the enterprise segment of a thousand employees-plus. (00:21:45): If you are not ready to go upmarket, I would say keep it easy on the product-led sales because sales means quotas. Sales means large contract values. Sales means you are going upmarket whether you like it or not, and some products, they should stay in the prosumer individual space. Maybe they're geared towards contractors or freelancers or squarely towards startups. Those persons are not interested in talking to sales in the first place. They have much lower bearing of how much they're willing to spend, so their price sensitivity is much higher. They prefer to do all self-serve in the first place, so it's really need to be conscious about what that will do to your go-to-market motion because it definitely skews it and pulls it up.
turns.zh: ……句号。意味着你追的合同金额，大概率高于你的"销售地板"——也就是销售愿意接、愿意关的最低值，传统上约 1.5 万美元。如果你追的是 1.5 万美元的合同，那你也大概率在尝试关 10 万、20 万美元的合同。谁扛得起 10 万、20 万的合同？不会是小创业公司，不会是 SMB，大概率是中高端市场的偏高段，也就是 200 人以上的公司；更可能是千人以上企业段。（00:21:45）如果你还没准备好上探市场，我会说产品驱动销售就先别碰，因为销售意味着配额、意味着大合同金额、意味着不管你乐不乐意你在上探市场。而有些产品就该待在 prosumer、个人空间——也许面向承包商、自由职业者、或就对准创业公司。那些人压根不想跟销售聊，他们愿意花的钱少得多，价格敏感度高，本来就偏好全自助。所以真得清醒认识到这会对你的 go-to-market 打法造成什么——它绝对会把它拉偏、往上拽。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it, so what I'm hearing is that if you're starting as a self-serve-oriented product and you're starting to maybe hire for a salesperson, is the approach start approaching it from product-led sales motion versus now we're going to add the sales independent team that's kind of doing their own thing?
turns.zh: 明白了。所以我听到的是：如果你从自助型产品起步、开始也许要招销售，打法是"从产品驱动销售切入"，而不是"现在加一个独立运作的销售团队"？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Right, so there's two ways to get to product-led sales. First little wave is that we talked about, I start as product-led growth company. I really started with this individual use case and I'm escalating to a company-level value prop and this is what I need product-led sales for. On the other side, I might start as a top-down sales traditional organization, so I have product that I only sell through sales. Those are usually anchored at larger segments in the first place. In order to build a top-down sales engine, you're most likely going after enterprise segment of a thousand-plus employees or maybe upper mid-market of 500 employees-plus. The reason to go into product-led sales is either your existing top-down motion is not working because customers need to see value before they sign the contract. They want to see that usage and at least the first signs of perceived value before they sign on the dotted line. (00:23:49): Or you're going downmarket and your fixed cost of sale that you have from the traditional sales motion does not scale. It stays fairly constant, yet your contract values are starting to drop as you're doing downmarket, so you want to create a lot more automation in the selling process to remove as many as possible humans out of it. You can approach it from both ways. Adding PLS on top of product-led growth or adding PLS on top of existing sales-led growth. For PLG, you're going upmarket by adding PLS. For SLG or sales-led growth, by adding PLS you're going downmarket.
turns.zh: 对，到产品驱动销售有两条路。第一波我们聊过：我从 PLG 公司起，真的是从个人用例开始、升级到公司级价值主张，这就是我需要产品驱动销售的地方。另一头，我可能从自上而下的传统销售组织起——产品只通过销售卖，通常一开始就锚定更大客群。要建自上而下的销售引擎，你大概率是追千人以上企业段、或 500 人以上的中上端市场。转做产品驱动销售的原因，要么是你现有的自上而下打法不灵——因为客户要签合同前先看到价值，他们想看到用量、至少感知价值的初步迹象，才肯签。（00:23:49）要么你在下探市场，而传统销售打法带来的固定销售成本不随规模下降，它基本恒定，可你下探时合同金额在跌，所以你想在销售流程里造更多自动化、尽可能去掉人力。两条路都能走：在 PLG 上加 PLS，或在现有销售驱动增长上加 PLS。对 PLG，靠加 PLS 上探市场；对 SLG（销售驱动增长），靠加 PLS 下探市场。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Awesome, and we're going to talk about how to actually build this infrastructure and what's required, but it reminds me one of the biggest takeaways from our first podcast and something I've quoted many times now, is your bet that every sales-led growth company needs to add a product-led growth element. Otherwise, they'll be disrupted by someone that does. Is that still your perspective?
turns.zh: 太棒了。我们待会儿聊怎么真建这套基础设施、需要什么。但这让我想起第一季最大的收获之一、我也引述过很多次：你的论断——每个销售驱动增长公司都得加一个产品驱动增长元素，否则会被这么做的人颠覆。这还是你的观点吗？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Absolutely. Now, I think there's different stages of, what does it mean to add product-led growth elements? I think every sales-led company should be putting pressure on product to assist with the sales process. That does not mean that there is product-led growth, but there is a product assist in the existing sales-led motion that can materialize into product-led growth if you can truly solve for self-serve activation, self-serve engagement, and have product be able to sell itself. The biggest difference here that starts to come in, and that is so apparent in every single company, is that in B2B, unfortunately, we've let go of the products having accountability over monetization model. We've gotten into the spiral of product just builds a product and it throws it over the fence to marketing and sales to sell. (00:25:38): Marketing and sales have done an incredible job over the last couple of decades of coming up with these stories and elaborate playbooks of how to attract enterprise buyers and how to sell them this product. Product literally only obsesses after contract is closed and there's usage that starts materialize after contract close. We've alleviated our product management in B2B from monetization ownership. When a SLG company actually goes into product-assisted tactics or product-led growth, the biggest pain point is actually educating product team on how can you get product to sell itself, which is all about monetization awareness, monetization friction of conversion to get into the paid plan, and then having actual correct value metrics that are understood self-serve by the customer. (00:26:29): I mean, yes, I agree with you. Every single... I agree with myself, so I should say that every single sales-led company should at least add some product-assisted tactics, but I would even take it further that every sales-led company should start educating and putting pressure on the product to own monetization components of the business.

For example, yesterday I've been adding one user per day and then today I've added 15 users to account. That's a velocity change that you need to pay attention to. Or there is a feature usage that can be highly correlative to enterprise interest. That product should be driving towards every single account reaching in order to qualify them for sales conversation. (00:30:00): Now, within the PQA, there may or may not be PQL, so PQL is a product-qualified lead. Lead assumes there is a person in the account that I can go and sell to. Now, leads are those buyers. User can make those buyer decisions. However, the more you move up the market, the more end user is many steps separated from the buyer, so you might have very healthy usage and you might have a PQA that is off the charts, but you don't have a PQL in it. (00:30:47): If you just stick your sales against that account, you're going to have a very terrible situation and very terrible user journey where users are like, "Why is sales talking to me? PQA can have a PQL as a user already in the user base, or you might need an MQL with marketing or sales, bringing their lead over and connecting them with the usage.

In traditional top-down sales book, an MQL that you have or a lead that you gather already is in consideration cycles for your enterprise-level offering. However, in product-led sales, a new user that signs up, they know we're close to enterprise-level consideration. They're just trying to complete an individual job to be done. They're not solving a problem for their company. If you can imagine, it is like a very large funnel. You start with just users looking for problem solve. Then, you transition to awareness, consideration, and intent channels for team level problem. Then, you escalate for awareness, consideration, and intent channels for enterprise-level problem. (00:34:41): Top-down sales process goes after the bottom of that funnel where there's already an intent to solve company-level problem versus at the very top is where product-led growth starts on individual-level problem. It's a different timeline. If you go after individual user that just signs up for the account and you reach out to them 10 minutes later after sign-up asking, "What's your budget and are you ready to buy?", it's a complete mismatch of where they are in their consideration journey. You cannot consider a new product sign-up an MQL in the traditional sense. They're just not there yet. They have a fraction of the enterprise problem that they're solving and they're not ready to buy.

You are not just dumping it on them and that you have a very strong feedback cycles from sales or whether what you've identified is correct or not correct because PQA definitions should not be static. They're constantly evolving. Just because it's right right now, that doesn't mean it's going to be right next quarter, so you have to have a lot of rituals with sales team to gather that feedback.
turns.zh: ……关于这个举手者、或关于从用量提交的销售表单，销售有多兴奋？你就从这开始。简单说：有多少其他账户在展现那些信号？当你的线索量还很低时，一开始别搞太复杂，要非常透明——就去理解销售看到了什么、对什么兴奋，然后把符合那模型的账户尽量喂给他们。唯一别做的事，就是一开始把每个用户都发给销售，因为那是最快让销售说"这产品渠道是垃圾，我再也不想看到这来的线索"的办法。他们的关单率和配额、薪水都系在能否关单上，于是他们直接把这当无效渠道无视了。（00:38:42）第二层升级是：好，你现在有直觉了，但来看看产品里"谁在举手"的实情。你看那些"看起来像、闻起来像、行为像举手者、但没真举手"的信号——那也许是个很简单的回归模型，可能只是个简单直方图分析：区分举手者和不举手者的差异，还有谁符合标准、基于那些差异看起来像举手者。（00:39:18）那该是你的第一个 PQA 模型，该很简单——比如你能对几个你注意到的高系数跑个线性回归，就知道哪个对可预测性权重最大，照那个来。关键是尽早让销售参与，跟他们合伙，而不是把东西往他们身上一倒；而且要从销售那拿强反馈循环，验证你识别的对不对，因为 PQA 定义不该是静态的，它持续演进。现在对，不代表下季度还对，所以你得跟销售团队有很多固定仪式来收集反馈。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: One thing I'll mention is Amplitude and Mixpanel both have a regression tool that help you identify correlations and causal kind of connections between metrics, so maybe shout-out there. I think it's called Compass-
turns.zh: 提一句：Amplitude 和 Mixpanel 都有回归工具，帮你识别指标间的相关和因果连接，也许喊一嘴。我想叫 Compass——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yep.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... and then Mixpanel's I think is called Signal.
turns.zh: ……Mixpanel 那个叫 Signal。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yep. Honestly, to be fair, most of the time I've done it manually at first because it requires so much understanding of the data, and if the data is correct and if I'm even seeing because you don't want to throw in too many co-related variables into the model because then you have issues of those variables like describing themselves, so to speak. Even if they're firing, there might not be actual predictive. It's partnership with analytics team and it's partnership with the intuition from the sales team. Then, you can start throwing it into a regression model and start to automate and think about scaling it, which there is a lot of PLS platforms that are coming up and finding their product-market fit at the moment that can do that for you. (00:41:04): I don't know if I would start there right from the beginning unless you actually understand the data because buying a platform will not bridge the gap for you understanding what actually matters in your data. Buying a platform or using a third-party solution will help you scale your efforts once you hit the first first, let's say, data sales fit that you can then scale and disincrease distribution of.
turns.zh: 对。坦白说，多数时候我一开始是手动做的，因为它太需要对数据的理解、以及数据对不对、我是不是真看到了——你不想往模型里塞太多相关变量，否则会有变量"自我描述"之类的问题。即便它们在触发，也可能并没有真正的预测力。这是和分析团队、和销售团队直觉的合伙。然后你才能丢进回归模型、开始自动化、想着规模化。现在有一批 PLS 平台正在冒头、找 product-market fit，能帮你做这事。（00:41:04）除非你真懂数据，否则我不会一开始就上那个——因为买个平台补不了你对"数据里什么才重要"的理解。买平台或用第三方方案，是在你达到第一个（姑且说）"data sales fit"、能放大分发之后，才帮你规模化努力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Data sales fit. Wow, that's a new term. There we go. I have not heard that before. Data sales fit. I love it, so you're saying basically start manually to make sure you fully understand what's going on?
turns.zh: Data sales fit（数据-销售契合）。哇，新词。来了。我之前没听过。Data sales fit。我太爱了。所以你说的本质是：先手动开始，确保你完全理解在发生什么？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: That's my take. Yeah. I-
turns.zh: 这是我的看法。对。我——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: [inaudible 00:41:42].

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... just... I don't... I have a hard time scaling something that I don't fully understand because data can tell you lies and you can just fit any story that you want into data. I need to really understand it and how it fits and what you are observing and that it makes sense before you go and start using automation on it.
turns.zh: ……就是……我……我很难去规模化一件我没完全理解的东西，因为数据会骗人，你能把任何想要的故事套进数据里。我得真懂它、懂它怎么契合、懂你在观察什么、而且它得讲得通，然后才去上自动化。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Cool. Okay, and then just one last question on what you were just talking about, which is finding correlations and causal relationships between usage and users and understanding who to send to sales. What are some common metrics and attributes that you've found that are indicative of they should go to sales?
turns.zh: 酷。好，关于你刚聊的——在用量和用户间找相关和因果关系、搞清楚该把谁发给销售——最后一个问题：你发现哪些常见指标和属性，是"该发给销售"的信号？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: One of the most important things is to create network effects within the company, within a team, which each additional team member added to an account benefits from everybody else. This does not mean you have to have platform network effects. You're not trying to be LinkedIn. You're not trying to be Instagram. Those are platform network effects. What you are trying to create is the value of each additional user into account. What that means, I'm going to go through slight deviation here is that there should not be only pulling mechanism where I pull you into my account. There also should be pushing mechanism. Any new sign-up that happens from the company that already has an account in my system should be presented with an option to join that account, not just create a brand new account. (00:43:06): What you don't want to create is hundreds of rogue individual accounts that don't know about each other. We as humans, we are creatures of community, we're creatures of we like to be surrounded by people, to be validated by people, and at least you want to create that herd mentality inside of the company and push and pull people into the account. One of the biggest PQAs is number of users in the company using your product. By the way, the magic number is usually seven. The more time you have seven or more users in the company and there's like some weird parallel here to seven friends at Facebook and seven collections at LinkedIn, but seven I've seen very often as a check mark. "Hey, there's enough value here distributed across multiple people inside the company that there might be an enterprise conversation to be had." (00:44:00): The second-most important is usually some sort of volume threshold. For example, for Amplitude, it's number of events that you're sending through, which means that you are really starting to tackle your entire application with analytics as opposed to just a small portion. Or with Miro, it was number of boards that you have in the account. With Figma, I think it's number of revisions that you have on any given design. The last one I would say is velocity. Velocity is the trickiest one just because we don't have a very easy way to measure velocity in our transactional data, but it's actually one of the most powerful one that triggers the right timing for the involvement because the change in velocity either number of users being added or events being sent or storage that is being utilized is usually a fantastic predictor.
turns.zh: 最重要的一件事，是在公司内、在团队内创造网络效应——每多一个团队成员加入账户，所有人都能从中受益。这不意味着你要有平台级网络效应，你不是要成为 LinkedIn、不是要成为 Instagram，那是平台网络效应。你要创造的是"每个新增用户给账户带来的价值"。意思是——我稍微岔开一下——不该只有"我把你拉进我的账户"这种拉的机制，也该有推的机制。任何来自已有账户公司的新注册，都该被给一个"加入那个账户"的选项，而不只是新建一个全新账户。（00:43:06）你不想造出几百个互不知晓的散兵账户。作为人，我们是群居生物、喜欢被人群包围、被人群认可，你至少要在公司里造出那种羊群心态，把人又推又拉进账户。最大的 PQA 之一，是公司里用你产品的人数。顺便，魔法数字通常是 7。公司里有 7 个或以上用户时——这里和 Facebook 的 7 个朋友、LinkedIn 的 7 个收藏有怪异的平行——但我常看到 7 是个分水岭："嘿，价值已经分散到公司里多个人身上了，也许能聊企业级了。"（00:44:00）第二重要的是某种用量门槛。比如 Amplitude 是发送的事件数——意味着你真的在拿分析去攻克整个应用，而不只是一小块。Miro 是账户里的白板数。Figma 我想是某个设计的修订数。最后一个是速度（velocity）。速度最棘手，只因我们在交易数据里没有很容易测速度的办法，但它其实是最强力的之一——它触发了"该介入"的正确时机，因为速度的变化（无论加用户、发事件、还是用存储）通常是极好的预测器。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Okay, so kind of like the simplest model to tell you there's a peak-y way is number of users usage and velocity.
turns.zh: 了不起。好，所以最简单的模型告诉你"有峰态"的，就是用户数、用量和速度。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yep-

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing.
turns.zh: 了不起。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... and users, by the way, can be either usage of velocity metric, too. It's just like if you're going to do anything, just look at whichever accounts have most users. It's like an 80-20 rule. For 20% of the efforts, you're probably going to get 80% of the value.
turns.zh: ……而且用户数，顺便，也可以是一个速度指标。就像你只要做点什么，就看哪些账户用户最多。像 80-20 法则：20% 的投入，你可能拿到 80% 的价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Love it. Okay, so I took us off track and you were talking about what data you may need in place. Is there anything else along those lines?
turns.zh: 爱了。好，我把话题带偏了，你刚在讲"需要什么数据就位"。这方面还有别的吗？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I would say that it's very important to identify behavioral signals as well, and I'll give an example. At Miro, we had a very strong behavioral signal that if there is an admin switch in the account, some sort of evaluation is happening. Admin transfer, new admin being assigned, that should be ding, ding, ding, all of the bells are ringing that you should maybe reach out to that person and see what's going on. The other one that is fascinating is your terms of use pages, your privacy and policy. Nobody cares about it unless they're considering enterprise deal. If you see anybody from account land on your terms of use pages, reach out to that person. More likely than not, you have a buyer on the hook and you can assist them in increasing their perceived value.
turns.zh: 我会说识别行为信号也非常重要，给个例子。在 Miro，我们有个很强的信号：账户里一旦发生管理员切换，就说明某种评估在进行。管理员转移、新管理员被指派——那该"叮叮叮"，所有铃都响，你也许该联系那个人、看看怎么回事。另一个很妙的是你的"使用条款"页、隐私政策页。没人在乎它，除非他们在考虑企业级deal。如果你看到账户里任何人落到使用条款页，联系那个人。十有八九，你钩上了一个买家，你能帮他们抬高感知价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, that is so interesting. That's the kind of stuff you only learn having done it.
turns.zh: 哇，太有意思了。这种事只有做过才学得会。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Many, many times, yes, but those-
turns.zh: 很多很多次，对，但那些——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh.
turns.zh: 哦。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... signals are, by the way, universal. We looked at it at MongoDB, it was very much true, so these things of when you... What in product constitutes evaluation process? What are the enterprise buyers are looking for? I wouldn't say, by the way, watching a webinar or landing on an enterprise landing page is a good behavioral signal because it might be annoying that I just like on accident landed on a landing page and now I'm being spammed by outbound SDR sequence. More meaningful actions that are deeper with an engagement user journey are incredible predictors.
turns.zh: ……信号，顺便，是通用的。我们在 MongoDB 看过，非常成立。所以这些——什么时候在产品里构成评估流程？企业买家在找什么？我不会说看个 webinar 或落到企业落地页是个好行为信号，因为我可能只是不小心落到落地页，现在就被外呼 SDR 序列 spam 了，那会很烦。更深、嵌入用户旅程的有意义动作，才是极好的预测器。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You talked again about this idea of spamming from sales and it made me think about like... I don't even know if I want to ask this, but have you seen downside to sales just continuing to hammer you as a potential user? Does that actually hurt? I don't want to know almost because I feel like the answer is no, but what do you think?
turns.zh: 你又聊到销售 spam 这事，让我想到……我甚至不确定要不要问，但你见过销售持续猛锤一个潜在用户的坏处吗？那真会伤害吗？我几乎不想知道答案，因为我觉得答案是"不会"，但你怎么看？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I think you have to look at the channel effectiveness. You have only so many channels to communicate with a customer. Email is obvious. You can communicate with them in app. You can have some sort of chatbot. Maybe you can deploy some sort of paid marketing, maybe social or retargeting display ads, but those are very expensive to utilize. Stepping back and thinking when it's the right time to reach out. How can I grab their attention? If you highly saturated the channel that is your primary for reaching out to the user, they're not going to react even if it's more of a right time for them to react. (00:47:59): Will it hurt you? I don't think you'll notice it right away, but over time I think people become blind to channel communication if it's not applicable to them because, "Fool me once, shame on you." Like, "Fine, you tricked me to opening this email." Fool me twice, it's shame on me and I'll be a lot more frugal of which emails I open or which notifications I react to. I think that you have to put user journey first and you have to really think about the timing that it's right for user and PQA. (00:48:34): All it is is the right time to engage with the customer and then go hit them hard over all of the channels of communication, but then, also know that accounts go in and out out of PQA. Today I might be in the PQA, next week I might not be, so you need to sunset the efforts if you didn't get in touch with the customer and wait for the next PQA moment. It will happen if your product is holding that goal and is accountable for getting more and more accounts to reach a threshold PQA.
turns.zh: 我觉得你得看渠道有效性。你和客户沟通的渠道就那么几个。邮件最明显；可以在 app 内沟通；可以有某种聊天机器人；也许能上点付费营销，社交或再营销展示广告，但那些用起来很贵。退一步想：什么时候联系才对？我怎么抓住他们注意力？如果你把"联系用户的主渠道"高度饱和了，哪怕对他们来说时机更对，他们也不会有反应。（00:47:59）它会伤害你吗？我觉得你不会马上注意到，但长期看，如果沟通不适用，人会对渠道沟通变盲——"骗我一次，是你丢人；我开了这邮件，行，你骗到我了。骗我两次，是我丢人"，于是我会更挑剔地决定开哪封邮件、对哪些通知有反应。我觉得你得把用户旅程放第一，真去想对用户和 PQA 都对的时机。（00:48:34）它全部就是"在正确时机接触客户，然后all渠道猛打"，但同时也要知道账户会进进出出 PQA——今天我在 PQA，下周可能不在，所以如果你没联系上客户，就该让努力 sunset（退场），等下一个 PQA 时刻。只要你的产品守着那目标、并为让越来越多账户达到 PQA 门槛负责，那一刻会再来。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, that's really interesting. I'm also happy to hear that answer. Great. Okay, so let's continue down this track of what it takes to implement a product-led sales motion. Just talked about the data component. What about just systems and infrastructure and tooling? What do you recommend there as a start?
turns.zh: 哇，真有意思。听到这答案我也挺高兴。好。好，我们顺着"落地一个产品驱动销售打法需要什么"继续。刚聊了数据部分。那系统和基础设施、工具呢？你建议从哪起步？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I approach the subject always as an evolution, not a revolution, so start with your existing systems as much as possible. I would say the biggest mistakes to avoid if your sales team is very heavily embedded into Salesforce, don't try to have them switch to a different solution. It's just not going to work. You need to try to figure out how to embed what you need the data into Salesforce, not get them to use some other third-party tool. Then, I wouldn't jump into any big commitments until I really prove out viability of product-led sales motion before automating any of it. I'm more of kind of Wizard of Oz it as fast as much as possible to get the initial traction so then we can validate that there is investment to be had in scaling it and there's a business value in it.
turns.zh: 我看待这事永远是演进、不是革命，所以尽量从你现有系统起。最大的坑要避开：如果你的销售团队深嵌在 Salesforce 里，别试图让他们换别的方案，那根本行不通。你得想办法把你需要的那些数据嵌进 Salesforce，而不是让他们用别的第三方工具。然后，在真证明产品驱动销售打法可行之前，我不会跳进任何大承诺、不会自动化任何东西。我更倾向"绿野仙踪式"——尽快用手动跑到初始牵引，这样我们才能验证：规模化这事值得投、有生意价值。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The tools you're using at that point, is it like Google Sheets? Or is there something else involved in [inaudible 00:50:17]-
turns.zh: 那阶段你用的工具，是像 Google Sheets 吗？还是有别的东西涉及（听不清 00:50:17）——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: It's-

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... Google Sheets, it's your Looker, Tableau dashboards, it's your Amplitude charts and reports. It can be widgets within Salesforce or ETLs that you pipe through HubSpot and Marketos into Salesforce, or it can be CRM solutions for PLG specifically that you literally deliver in Excel sheets to sales team to prototype a different outreach.
turns.zh: ……Google Sheets、你的 Looker、Tableau 看板、你的 Amplitude 图表和报告。可以是 Salesforce 里的小组件，或是你通过 HubSpot、Marketos 灌进 Salesforce 的 ETL，也可以是专为 PLG 的 CRM 方案——你 literal 用 Excel 表把东西递给销售团队，去原型化一种不同的触达。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Have you shared any of this kind of like MVP product-led sales stack that you recommend? If not, I think you should because that seems pretty useful.
turns.zh: 你有没有分享过你推荐的这种 MVP 版产品驱动销售技术栈？没有的话，我觉得你该分享，看起来挺有用。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yeah, I think I definitely should.
turns.zh: 对，我觉得我确实该。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: All right, there we go.
turns.zh: 好，那就成了。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I have my idea for a next blog post. Done.
turns.zh: 我下篇博客的点子有了。搞定。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There we go. Okay. If we got anything out of this chat, we've got that. Okay, in terms of people, so we talked about data, we talked about tooling, infrastructure, what do you suggest in terms of people and resources to invest in this area as a start, and then also as you evolve?
turns.zh: 那就成了。好。如果说这聊天有任何产出，就是这个了。好，说到人——我们聊了数据、聊了工具基础设施，起步时你建议在"人和资源"上投什么？以及演进时呢？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: For PLS, the people that you need is product managers that will be able to get account to PQA stage. You will need salespeople that will understand which usage triggered PQA and how to apply that information to find a buyer and to enable a buyer to convert them to an opportunity. You need marketing to educate both the end user or enterprise buyer on why the value of this enterprise solution is going to make sense to you, and you need analytics team. You need a data analyst that will continuously dig in the data to find correlative signals that you can test causation in. Those are the four people that you need, product, analytics, marketing, sale. I should say engineering, too, obviously, but I'm kind of bundling them together with product, (00:52:05): Now, it's an evolution, not a revolution, so if you're starting from sales-led growth, I would highly suggest of you going to a sales team and asking for somebody to run a pilot with you. Don't just throw these leads into the top-down sales process and assume that everything is going to be just fine. Attach to yourself a pilot AE, so account executive, or an SDR and see how that works. You kind of separate yourself from the mothership of the sales engine and you actually prototype this separately in a little bit of a vacuum, not under pressure of them top-down quota relief. If you in a product-led growth company, then I would suggest do your own sales. It's kind of like a founder-led growth, so think about it like, "Hey, you need to close maybe first couple of deals you sell first so you truly understand what's happening," and would not get first hand-raisers and say, "Oh, we can't close it unless we have a salesperson." (00:53:01): No, just have somebody support to do it. Have somebody on finance do it. You do it. I've been on chat myself plenty of times trying to close the deals just to understand what's the sales process for the customers looks like. Then, you can figure out who to actually hire and who to actually scale, but for PLS that starts in PLG, you actually just start with more of blend of an SZR and AE together because you don't need two separations. The same person can both outbound to a customer and close them at the same time, and then you can go into specialization of the role. Start small, start nimble, prove it out, scale along the way, but have marketing and analytics support you the entire journey.
turns.zh: 做 PLS，你需要的人，是能让账户到达 PQA 阶段的产品经理；你需要销售——他们得懂"什么用量触发了 PQA"、怎么用那信息去找买家、赋能买家把他们转成机会；你需要营销去教育终端用户或企业买家"为什么这企业方案的价值对你说得通"；你还需要分析团队——一个数据分析师，持续挖掘数据、找相关信号，好去测因果。这是你需要的四拨人：产品、分析、营销、销售。工程当然也算，但我把它跟产品捆一起了。（00:52:05）这是演进不是革命，所以如果你从销售驱动增长起，我强烈建议去找销售团队、要个人跟你跑个 pilot。别直接把这些线索丢进自上而下销售流程、假设一切都会好。给自己配一个 pilot AE（客户经理）或 SDR，看它怎么运作。你有点脱离销售引擎的"母舰"，在一点真空里单独原型化，不被自上而下配额压力压着。如果你在 PLG 公司，我建议你自己做销售——有点像 founder-led growth。想成"嘿，你得自己关掉头几单，才能真正理解在发生什么"，而不是抓到第一个举手者就说"哦，没销售我们关不了"。不，就找个人支持着做，让财务的人做，你自己做。我自己就常上聊天去关单，就为理解客户的销售流程长什么样。然后你才知道该招谁、该规模化谁。但对"从 PLG 起步的 PLS"，你其实从 SDR 和 AE 混合起步就行，因为不需要两拨分开——同一个人既能外呼又能关单，之后你再让角色专业化。从小起、从灵起、证明它、沿途规模化，但让营销和分析全程支持你。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is really simple. What I'm hearing is you don't need to hire someone new necessarily. You have the resources most likely, and then it's just, how do you allot some time of this team to start investing and violating?
turns.zh: 真简单。我听到的是：你不一定需要招新人，资源你大概率已经有了，只是怎么分这块团队的时间、开始投入和"violating"（试错）？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yeah, I'd say that my philosophy is that I want to have an ROI for a new hire before putting a job rec out there, and to create an ROI, I need to prove it out of what potential can there be myself first. I can almost like fund this hire with the revenue that we can generate out of this channel originally. Obviously that includes a lot of individual contributor work that you have to do in the area potentially that is not comfortable, but that's the fastest way to grow in your career, so I think that's a necessary step for a successful execution.
turns.zh: 对，我会说我的理念是：在发招聘帖前，我想先对新招的人有 ROI；而要造出 ROI，我得先自己证明这事有多大潜力。我几乎能用这渠道最初产生的营收，去给这个 hire 供资。当然那包括很多你可能不舒服的个人贡献者工作，但那是你职业成长最快的路，所以我认为那是成功执行的必要一步。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You want to hear a crazy stat about product-led growth and not hiring sales?
turns.zh: 想听个关于 PLG、以及"不招销售"的疯狂数据吗？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Sure.
turns.zh: 当然。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, great. I was chatting with the founder of Notion for the series I'm working on and Notion didn't hire their first salesperson until they were past 10 million ARR.
turns.zh: 好，太棒了。我正在做的那个系列里，跟 Notion 创始人聊过，Notion 直到 ARR 过 1000 万才招第一个销售。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I believe it. Miro did not hire their first salesperson until they were like 5 or 7 million in ARR. They were literally closing the contracts through support team and it was just fine.
turns.zh: 我相信。Miro 也是到 ARR 大概 500 万或 700 万才招第一个销售。他们 literal 是通过支持团队关合同，完全没问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Same with Notion, it was their customer success and support team.
turns.zh: Notion 也一样，是他们的客户成功和支持团队。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yep.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is some product-led growth right there.
turns.zh: 这就是 PLG 该有的样子。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love it. Amazing. Okay, so we've talked about data, tooling, people. Is there anything else that you find is really important to being successful with rolling out a product-led sales bridge motion?
turns.zh: 爱了。了不起。好，我们聊了数据、工具、人。还有没有什么是你觉得对成功铺开"产品驱动销售桥梁打法"特别重要的？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: The most important thing in product-led sales is that there is a different configuration internally of collaboration that needs to occur. In traditional sales world, marketing creates pipeline for sales. Sales sells product. Product engages with a paid user to drive retention. In the product-led sales, product acquires and activates a customer and product creates pipeline for sales. Relationship is not that there's a go-to-market org with marketing and sales, and product just kind of throws features across the fence for them to sell. (00:55:59): The collaboration here is between product and sales, but that means the product has to take on accountability over pipeline. The worst thing that you can do is to say, "I'm going to do product-led growth," or, "I'm going to do product-led sales and I'm going to do it in marketing." Recipe for disaster. You'll be failure mode within six months because product has to take accountability over selling of the product itself. That is not to be taken lightly because so many product teams are deeply, deeply uncomfortable with owning monetization targets. Now, I'm not saying that product should just be gold and revenue because that's a very short-term short outcome past performance. There has to be a very clear designation onto long-term goals and long-term objectives and revenue ownership. (00:56:52): By revenue ownership, I don't mean that individual product manager also should have a revenue target on their back. What I mean is that the product leadership should be accountable for the revenue target, but the product people should be responsible for more of KPIs, free to paid conversion rate, package mix, PQA, maybe even PQLs, but those are all of the KPIs into revenue. The piece to me that is of utmost importance is to keep product accountable. You cannot start this product-led stales motion in marketing and sales and think that it can continue with the same configuration inside the company and still succeed. Product has to have a seat at the table and product has to feel accountable and responsible for it.
turns.zh: 产品驱动销售里最重要的事，是内部需要一种不同的协作配置。传统销售世界里，营销为销售创造管道，销售卖产品，产品跟付费用户互动来驱动留存。而在产品驱动销售里，产品负责获取并激活客户、还替销售创造管道——关系不是"有个 go-to-market 组织，营销和销售在那，产品只是把功能扔过墙让他们去卖"。（00:55:59）这里的协作是产品与销售之间，但这意味着产品方必须承担起"管道"的责任。你能做的最糟的事就是："我要做产品驱动增长"或"我要做产品驱动销售，而且我要放在营销里做。"那是灾难配方。半年内就会失败，因为产品必须对自己产品的销售负责。这不能轻描淡写，因为太多产品团队对"背变现目标"深、深地不舒服。现在我不是说产品就该只盯营收金和收入，因为那是基于过往表现的极短期结果。必须非常清楚地指定长期目标和长期目的，以及营收所有权。（00:56:52）说到营收所有权，我不是说每个产品 PM 背上也得有个营收目标。我的意思是：产品领导层该为营收目标负责，但产品人员该对更多 KPI 负责——免费到付费的转化率、套餐组合、PQA、也许甚至 PQL——但那些全是指向营收的 KPI。对我而言最重要的那块，是让产品保持可问责。你不能在营销和销售里启动这个产品驱动销售打法、还以为它能以公司里同样的配置继续、还能成功。产品必须在桌上有席、必须感到对这事可问责、负责任。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: When you say accountable, what does that actually look like? Is it like their OKRs have certain goals around, "Here's how many PQAs you're driving?" Is it a number? What does accountable mean in this-
turns.zh: 你说"可问责"，实际长什么样？是他们的 OKR 有某些目标，像"你驱动的 PQA 数量"？是个数字吗？可问责在这指什么——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I think so. Every product has some sort of goals and they definitely should have goals on keeping healthy, engaged user base. They should definitely have goals in terms of maybe feature utilization or customer satisfaction, but what I'm saying is to have also some sort of monetization goals. What that is for each company, I think, differs depending on their level of comfort and how close they are to revenue capture mechanism. Let's say at Miro, our head of growth product had a self-serve revenue target on her back. She drove it. She had revenue goal that she had to hit in product and she shared marketing because I ran marketing in that company. We shared a pipeline goal creation because pipeline cannot be created without marketing, too. (00:58:33): Marketing will need to educate. Marketing will need to find the buyer. Marketing will need to do accounts-based marketing in order to attract the buyer and connect it with the usage. Product and marketing now pull together to create the pipeline and give it to sales, but product can no longer sit on this island as a feature factory. It only works with the top-down sales organizations, which, as I said, I think are going to be heavily disrupted over the next 10 years with value-first product-led growth.
turns.zh: 我认为是。每个产品都有某种目标，它们绝对该有"保持健康、有参与的用户群"的目标，绝对该有功能利用率或客户满意度这类目标，但我想说的是：还得有某种变现目标。那对每家公司具体是什么，我觉得取决于他们对营收捕获机制的舒适度、以及离它多近。比如 Miro，我们的增长产品负责人背着一个自助营收目标，她驱动它。她在产品上有必须达成的营收目标，而她跟我（我在那公司管营销）共享，因为我们共享一个管道创造目标——因为没有营销，管道也造不出来。（00:58:33）营销需要去教育、需要去找买家、需要做基于客户的营销（ABM）来吸引买家、把它连上用量。现在产品和营销一起拉、共同创造管道、交给销售——但产品再也不能坐在孤岛上当功能工厂。那只跟自上而下的销售组织配合，而那种组织，如我所说，未来十年会被"价值优先的产品驱动增长"重度颠覆。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is another hilarious meme that you shared on your LinkedIn, so another reminder, go check out Elena's LinkedIn with this hilarious meme of product teams being presented, "Hey, you're going to own some revenue targets." They're like, "Oh no." Yeah, exactly.
turns.zh: 这是你在 LinkedIn 分享的另一张好笑梗图，再提醒一次：去看 Elena 的 LinkedIn，有张产品团队被告知"嘿，你要背点营收目标了"、然后"哦不"的梗图。对，正是。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: It's actually super interesting because a lot of growth leaders shy away from revenue targets. Acquisition target, sure. Retention target, engagement target, sure, but monetary target, "Oh no. How can I possibly own a revenue target?" I think we all in tech, and I specifically point a finger at my industry in B2B industry, just got a little bit complacent with revenue ownership from product side. I do think it's catastrophic for us in the long term if we don't fix it.
turns.zh: 这其实超有意思，因为很多增长负责人对营收目标退避三舍。获客目标？行。留存目标、参与目标？行。但金钱目标？"哦不，我怎么可能背营收目标？"我觉得我们科技圈——我特别指我所在的 B2B 行业——在产品侧的营收所有权上有点自满了。我真觉得，如果不修，长期是灾难性的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love it. I want to do a whole podcast on your meme strategy and your parodies that you put out, but we'll stay on track here. In terms of the revenue target, what is that goal like? Is it just in this quarter X million dollars of revenue? Is it a growth rate from quarter over quarter? How do you find people actually define that revenue target?
turns.zh: 爱了。我很想单独做一期聊你的梗图策略和那些 parody，但我们还是回到主线。说到营收目标，那目标长什么样？就"本季度 X 百万美元营收"？还是季度环比增长率？你怎么找人真去定义那个营收目标？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Right, so there's different targets that you would have for self-serve revenue versus product-led sales revenue. For self-serve revenue, your KPIs should absolutely be free to paid conversion rates or trial to paid conversion rate. It's the package mix, it's the average revenue per user or ARPU. It may be retention rates, first-term retention rate, second-term retention rate in order for you to sustain the healthy revenue. That's what outputs self-serve revenue. Those should be the pieces. Do I have a problem in friction and acquiring new paid user in maximizing their value or in retaining that paid user? Those are the three inputs that go into self-serve ARR targets, and you should just understand where the biggest opportunity for your team to focus on driving it. (01:00:56): In any of those cases, most of the time free to pay conversion is the biggest focus of any given team just because we want to better convert and inflow into our user base, assuming we have good product-market fit so we have a solid retention happening. In free to pay conversion, there's three pillars that you constantly need to work on, and one pillar dominates them all. It's monetization awareness. Simple as that. If you have a freemium product, I guarantee you 75% of your customers in freemium product are not aware of what you're selling. Only focusing on monetization awareness can give you incredible output on driving monetization, and it's really it's product's ability to communicate via feature walls, via usage walls, via trials, or what the value of the paid offering is. (01:01:50): I've heard stories from Slack of just showing message limits and how big of an improvement on conversion rate it had. I've had it firsthand at SurveyMonkey where just adding consistent EUI across all of the paid triggers that were that Amazon gold color and making sure that each user has been able to see at least three of them. There's a rule of three that goes into advertising that we need to see things three times in order to remember them that drove monetization awareness and conversion rate up, but that's basically consumers 80% of your work. The second one is just conversion rate optimization, so your pricing page optimization, your checkout page optimization, your currencies that you offer, the payment methods that you offer to make sure that there's as little friction as possible in order to actually pay. (01:02:39): Then, the last one is what you're selling, do people want to buy? This is where you actually go after monetization model change. Which features are in each plan? What are the price points in each plan? How did the upgrade path look like? Do you have add-on strategy? DO you have just pay-to-pay fee monetization plan strategy? That one is like the last one that you should cross because it involves a lot of cross-functional effort and decision-making, but free to paid conversion, upsell potential, and retention. That's for self-serve AR. For product-led sales, what product should own is PQA, but who defines PQA? That's the big question. (01:03:19): Who iterates on PQA? Then, how do you actually get people to get to the PQA stage? Just like product often will own engagement metric or maybe even activation target, your own PQA target, so that just becomes one of the goals. Depending on where the biggest effort that needs to be, it can be an activation, it can be engagement in PPPQA, but more and more I see product-led, especially mature companies needing to focus their product teams on PQQ, yet they don't have a clear definition because sales kind of goes rogue and does their own thing. Product fails to deliver predictable pipeline to sales, which pushes sales into a top-down motion prematurely.
turns.zh: 对，自助营收和产品驱动销售营收，目标不同。自助营收的 KPI 绝对该是免费到付费的转化率、或试用到付费的转化率；是套餐组合、是 ARPU（每用户平均收入）；可能是留存率、首期留存、二期留存，好维持健康营收。那才是自助营收的产出，这些该是组成块。我在获取新付费用户、最大化其价值、或留存那付费用户上，哪有摩擦问题？这是输入自助 ARR 目标的三个输入，你只需搞清团队最该聚焦哪块去驱动它。（01:00:56）那些情形里，多数时候免费到付费转化是任何团队最大的焦点，只因我们假设有好的 product-market fit、有扎实留存，所以想更好转化、把人流入用户群。在免费到付费转化里，有三个你持续要做的支柱，其中一个主导一切：变现意识（monetization awareness）。就这么简单。如果你有 freemium 产品，我保证 75% 的 freemium 客户根本不知道你在卖什么。只聚焦变现意识，就能在驱动变现上给你惊人产出——而它本质上是产品通过功能墙、用量墙、试用，去沟通"付费方案的价值是什么"的能力。（01:01:50）我听过 Slack 的故事——就展示消息上限，转化率就有多大提升。我在 SurveyMonkey 亲身经历过——给所有付费触发点都加上一致的 EUI（那个亚马逊金色调），并确保每个用户至少看到其中三个。广告里有个"三遍法则"：一个东西得看三遍才记得住——这就把变现意识和转化率拉起来了。但这基本占你 80% 的活。第二是转化率优化（CRO）：定价页优化、结账页优化、你提供的币种、你提供的支付方式，尽量让真正付款的摩擦最小。（01:02:39）最后一个是"你卖的东西，人们想买吗？"——这才是你真正去动变现模型的地方：每个套餐里有哪功能？每个套餐什么价位？升级路径长啥样？你有附加组件策略吗？有按量付费的变现计划策略吗？这个最该放最后动，因为它涉及大量跨职能努力和决策。但免费到付费转化、增购潜力、留存——这是自助 ARR。对产品驱动销售，产品该拥有的是 PQA，但谁定义 PQA？那是大问题。（01:03:19）谁迭代 PQA？然后你怎么真让人到达 PQA 阶段？就像产品常会拥有参与度指标、甚至激活目标——你也拥有你自己的 PQA 目标，于是它就成了目标之一。取决于最大精力在哪，它可以是激活、可以是 PQA 里的参与，但我越来越看到产品驱动（尤其成熟公司）需要把产品团队聚焦在 PQA 上，可他们没清晰定义，因为销售有点"各行其是"，产品没能给销售交付可预测的管道，反而把销售过早推回自上而下打法。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A PQA target would be like 1,000 PQAs at this quarter. Is that the way you-
turns.zh: PQA 目标会是像"本季度 1000 个 PQA"？是这种吗——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yeah, yeah, so you usually actually look at it almost from conversion rate. You look at, "Okay, how many teams do I have in my ICP, so ideal customer profile segment, that are active?" That's my denominator, and how many of those teams are reaching PQA target-
turns.zh: 对对，你通常其实从转化率看它。你看"好，我的 ICP（理想客户画像）里有多少团队是活跃的？"那是分母，其中多少团队达到 PQA 目标——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Mm-hmm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... this month? It's like a conversion rate to PQA out of engaged ICP teams.
turns.zh: ……这个月？就像从"参与中的 ICP 团队"到 PQA 的转化率。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: One thing that I love that you've touched on is this awareness of monetization.
turns.zh: 你提到的一点我超爱：对变现的意识。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: People knowing that you have more features and that you may get access to more if you pay. How do you track that? Is it just like people seeing it per account or per user, like what percentage of seeing one of these upsells or seeing them three times?
turns.zh: 人们知道你有更多功能、知道付费能解锁更多。你怎么追踪这个？是按账户或按用户"看到过"的百分比吗？比如看到过这些增购之一、或看到过三次的比例？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I track it fairly simple two ways, one, qualitatively. I just run surveys against people and say, "Do you know what we're selling?" It's shocking how many just have no idea what's in our paid plans. Like we have major issue here, or I just track pricing page views per activated account. How many of the activated accounts landed on the pricing page at least once? That's at least a level of exposure that they hit some sort of trigger that pulled them to explore a pricing page. One of the things that just want to give a hint to anybody who's listening from a sales top-down companies, one issue you might have is that when your products is developing functionality, especially paid functionality, they just design review it and ship it for paid plans only. (01:05:34): If I'm in the free plan or in the lower tier plan, I don't even see it. I don't even know of it existence because it doesn't exist in the app because it was never designed for me to even see it. Just doing one small change of pushing your design reviews to review functionality from every single state of the customer, free state, lower paid state, and target state that this functionality is actually unlocked can do all of the difference in the world. Then, you'll actually understand how that [inaudible 01:06:06] functionality is being exposed to a free user, so them to become aware in self-serve manner of its existence.
turns.zh: 我跟踪得很简单，两种方式，一是定性。我就给用户发问卷问"你知道我们在卖什么吗？"震惊的是好多人根本不知道付费计划里有啥——"我们这有大问题"——或者我就追踪"每激活账户的定价页浏览量"：多少激活账户至少落到定价页一次？那至少说明他们触发了某种东西、被拉去探索定价页。想给听众所里来自自上而下销售公司的人一个提示：你可能会有的一个问题是——当你的产品在做功能（尤其付费功能）时，他们只在设计评审后、只给付费计划发货。如果你在免费计划或低档计划，你根本看不到它、根本不知道它存在，因为它从没被设计成让你看到。（01:05:34）只做一个小改动——把设计评审推到"从客户的每个状态（免费态、低付费态、目标态）去评审这个功能是否真的被解锁"——就能造成天壤之别。然后你才真理解这功能怎么被暴露给免费用户，让他们以自助方式意识到它存在。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love, love, love all these little tactical little insights and tips, so thanks for sharing all these little things that end up being the most useful to people. Just a few more questions and then I'll let you go. One is around pitfalls. What have you found are the most common pitfalls that startups run into as they're trying to invest in product-led sales? You touched on a few, but what comes to mind when I ask you that?
turns.zh: 我太爱这些小战术洞察和小贴士了，谢谢你分享这些最后对人最有用的东西。再几个问题就放你走。一个是关于坑。你发现创业公司在投入产品驱动销售时，最常见的坑是什么？你提过几个，但问到这你脑子里冒出来的是什么？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Let's just go through some summary that we've mentioned already throughout our conversation. Don't treat PLS as a traditional top-down sales process. Every single user does not equal. It's a opportunity for you to co-chase after. You need to understand the right triggers and usage. They can help you automate qualification process, so it's almost automating some of the SDR efforts to say, "When is the right time for my sales, for my human that I'm paying a lot of money, to intervene into this account and add value?" (01:07:13): Sales interaction has to add value to user journey, not be disruptive or create additional friction because I've seen so many, even people posting of like, "Why am I getting a phone call 10 minutes later" It's annoying. I'm going to stop using the product because of it." They feel misunderstood. For that profile. Your customers understand whether you have buyers, whether you have users, and they're in your ICP segment. Know this information upfront so you can serve a best experience possible. (01:07:44): Number two, hold your product accountable. This cannot be just executed through marketing and sales. Product has to have a seat at the table and product and sales relationship has to be one of the closest ones in this motion. That's really hard to change, especially in the traditional top-down sales company where marketing and sales have closer relationship. Try to create new rituals. Try to create the new ways of communication between the teams for them to be aligned behind the same goals. (01:08:16): Number three, don't leave marketing out of the equation. Majority of your usage will not have a buyer in it. You will need marketing, your enterprise marketing, your account-based marketing to go and find and hunt that buyer and to bring them and connect them with usage. Lean on your marketing team. Just because you're doing product-led growth and product-led sales does not mean you don't need marketing, and strong product marketer can do wonders here in helping you with messaging, with outreach, and sales enablement materials. (01:08:48): Number three, don't wait on data efficacy too long. You might be using your intuition at the beginning very well, but start thinking about how you will need to scale your data issues because product-led sales is all about leveraging usage for pipeline creation. You need to be able to measure that usage, understand that usage, track it, and evolve it.
turns.zh: 我们就过几个对话里已经提过的总结。一，别把 PLS 当传统自上而下销售流程。每个用户都不等于"一个你可以去追的机会"。你需要理解正确的触发和用量——它们能帮你自动化资格流程，就像自动化一部分 SDR 的努力，去说"我的销售、我花大钱雇的人，什么时候该介入这个账户、去加值？"（01:07:13）销售互动必须给用户旅程加值，而不是打断、或制造额外摩擦——我见过太多人发帖"为什么注册 10 分钟后就接到电话"，很烦，"我要因此不用这产品了"。他们觉得被误解。对那种画像，你的客户得懂：你有买家吗、有用户吗、他们在你的 ICP 段吗？提前知道这些信息，你才能给最好的体验。（01:07:44）二，让产品可问责。这不能只通过营销和销售执行。产品必须在桌上有席，而在这打法里，产品和销售的关系必须是最紧密的关系之一。这很难改，尤其在传统自上而下销售公司——那里面营销和销售关系更近。试着造新仪式、造团队间新的沟通方式，让他们对齐在同一目标后。（01:08:16）三，别把营销排除在外。你绝大多数用量里没有买家。你需要营销、你的企业营销、你的 ABM，去找到、去猎那个买家、把他带来、连上用量。倚重你的营销团队。只因为你做 PLG 和 PLS，不代表你不需要营销——一个强的产品营销人，能在信息、触达、销售赋能材料上创造奇迹。（01:08:48）四，别在"数据效能"上等太久。你开始时用直觉用得很好，但要开始想你该怎么规模化你的数据问题，因为产品驱动销售全是关于借用量来造管道。你得能量它、懂它、追踪它、演进它。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing. Two more things. One is you shared before we started chatting that you have some benchmarks around some of these metrics that you've mentioned of just what is good so that people can understand what their goals might be. What can you share there?
turns.zh: 了不起。还有两件。一是你开聊前分享过，你对提到的某些指标有些基准（benchmark），让人知道目标大概该是什么。那你能分享点什么？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yes, so in terms of benchmarks, first of all, it's time to get from individual usage, when that user comes in to have a single job to be done, to creating an enterprise-level contract. It does not happen in hours. It does not happen in days. It doesn't even happen in months of usage. A couple of benchmarks for y'all across Netlify, Miro, or Amplitude, which are all of the companies I worked at. It was 12 months plus of usage that had to happen before sales contracts can be created on sustainable way. (01:10:02): Now, that's not an all-encompassing rule. You will have very high-intent buyers coming in sometimes and you'll be able to close them within a week, but on average it takes a year of usage to escalate the problem from individual to a company-level solution. It takes time, be patient. This is not the problem of get more sign-ups this quarter and close more pipeline in the same quarter. This says you building for long-term growth and you closing contracts and the sign-ups that happened really last year in the best case scenario. (01:10:36): Number two is don't confuse user and buyer. Please, please, please profile your users upon sign-up. Do not skip those onboarding questions. No, they do not detract for your onboarding completion rates and people that do drop off in the profiling stage, they were low intent anyways. They were never going to be activating if one extra question deterred them from completing, from continuing with your product. Profile your people, know who you're talking to. It's more important than a couple percentage drop-off that will never going to activate in the first place. No, no, no die user please because all of us-
turns.zh: 对，说到基准，首先，从"个人用量"——那个用户进来、有个要完成的任务——到"创造企业级合同"，这时间不是几小时、不是几天、甚至不是几个月的用量。在 Netlify、Miro、Amplitude（都是我待过的公司）那几个基准是：得有 12 个月以上的用量，才能可持续地造出销售合同。（01:10:02）这不是包罗万象的规则。你偶尔会有高意向买家进来、一周内关掉，但平均来说，把问题从个人升级到公司级方案要一年的用量。要时间，耐心点。这不是"本季度搞更多注册、同季度关更多管道"的问题。这是为长期增长而建、你关的合同和注册，最好情况下是去年发生的。（01:10:36）二是别混淆用户和买家。求求求，注册时就给用户画像。别跳过那些 onboarding 问题。不，它们不会拉低你的 onboarding 完成率——在画像阶段流失的人，本来意向就低。如果一个额外问题就把他们劝退、不再继续用你的产品，他们本来也不会激活。给你的用户画像、知道你在跟谁谈。这比那几个百分点的流失重要得多——反正那些人本来也不会激活。别、别、别在用户上 die，因为我们所有人——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I like that.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这点。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... are tired of receiving outbound that is not relevant to us. Then, the third one is conversion. Conversion rates here actually stand from the true PLG companies, so freemium conversion rate is usually around 5%, trial conversions are more closer to 10 to 15%, but your contract value start to go up. (01:11:40): It's not so much that you increasing conversion rates because a lot of those companies will still go through self-serve monetization flow before they become your sales pipeline prospects. Conversion rates stay the same, but your contract values and your lifetime value of the customer is what starts to increasingly go up and that you can influx into creating a smile revenue curve.
turns.zh: ……都厌倦了收到跟我们不相干的冷外呼。第三是转化。这里的转化率其实来自真正的 PLG 公司：freemium 转化率通常约 5%，试用转化更接近 10% 到 15%，但你的合同金额开始往上走。（01:11:40）你不是主要在提转化率，因为很多这类公司在成为你销售管道潜客前，仍会走自助变现流程。转化率基本不变，但你的合同金额和客户的终身价值开始不断往上——而那你能灌进、造出一条微笑的营收曲线。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Incredible. The question you had about profiling your user, I was going to ask what questions to ask. I'm guessing maybe a better approach is just go to Miro or Amplitude and just go through the sign-in flow and see what they're asking.
turns.zh: 难以置信。你那个给用户的画像问题，我正要问该问什么。我猜更好的办法是直接去 Miro 或 Amplitude，走一遍注册流程，看他们问什么。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Yeah, I would give some couple parameters in place. Number one, limited to maybe three to four screens because otherwise it starts to feel too long. Make sure they only ask information that you either going to use in the data segmentation that then you can escalate to personalization and messaging, but at least that you're going to use on data segmentation and experiment with how deep of an information that you can ask. (01:12:36): You should always be able to ask about company size, about the department, which customers coming from, about their seniority on the team and about their use case. Those four questions are uniform. Everybody's used to answering them. The rest like phone number or some... maybe if you need to know the address or so on, those experiments, how much you actually want to make them required questions versus optional, but please, please, please experiment on your onboarding questionnaires. All of you.
turns.zh: 对，我会给几个参数。第一，限制在大概三到四个屏，否则就开始显得太长。确保他们只问你要么会用（用于数据分群、然后能升级到个性化与信息触达）、要么至少会用在数据分群、并实验"你能问多深的信息"上的那些信息。（01:12:36）你总该能问公司规模、问部门（客户来自哪个部门）、问他们在团队里的层级、问他们的用例。那四个问题是一致的——所有人都习惯回答。其余像电话号码或地址之类的，是你实验"你实际想把它们设成必答还是选答"的地方。但求求求，去实验你们的 onboarding 问卷。你们所有人。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Closing question. Everyone started with sales, sales-led growth. and then product-led growth emerged and now there's this bridge between the two of sales-led growth. Feels like there's always this new way of growing a business and approaching go-to-market. Is there something beyond product-led sales? What's next, if anything?
turns.zh: 收尾问题。大家都从销售、销售驱动增长起家，然后产品驱动增长浮现，现在这两者之间有了这座桥。感觉总有一种新的增长和 go-to-market 方式在冒出来。产品驱动销售之后还有什么吗？如果有的话，下一步是什么？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Well, I wonder how much a rise in AI is going to automate some of those sales conversations. It's not going to be truly product-led growth because-
turns.zh: 嗯，我好奇 AI 的崛起会在多大程度上自动化一部分那些销售对话。它不会是真正的产品驱动增长，因为——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: No shit.
turns.zh: 可不是。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... it's not like just the product's it's going to sell itself. What if on the other side of that chat or other side of that email or even a Zoom call because they can do a deep fake of anybody, it's going to be AI selling to you and giving you very deep and personalized answers? I am curious to see how that's going to evolve because the plethora of information that AI can surface to you in a very personalized manner in a matter of seconds is far stronger than any human or even content management system can do at the moment.
turns.zh: ……不是产品自己卖自己那种。但如果那聊天、那邮件、甚至那 Zoom 电话的另一头——因为他们能 deepfake 任何人——是 AI 在卖给你、给你极深极个性的回答呢？我很好奇这会怎么演进，因为 AI 能在几秒内以极个性的方式浮现给你的海量信息，比现在任何人、甚至任何内容管理系统都强得多。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you want to coin an acronym right now for what that might be?
turns.zh: 你想现在给那可能是什么造个缩写吗？

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Have to be AI sales.
turns.zh: 得是 AI 销售（AI sales）。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: A-I-S-L-
turns.zh: A-I-S-L——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: There I go.
turns.zh: 这就来了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... G. Wow, it's a mouthful. Elena, this was everything I was hoping it would be. I imagine this episode will be even more popular than your first one. Thank you so much for making time and getting into such detail in all the things we talked about. Two final questions. Where can folks find online if they want to reach out, learn more? How can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: ……G。哇，好拗口。Elena，这期就是我希望的一切。我猜这期会比你第一季还火。非常感谢你抽时间、把我们聊的所有东西都钻得这么细。最后两个问题：大家想在线找到你、想联系、想多了解，去哪？听众又能怎么帮到你？

turns.en: I'm on LinkedIn a lot, but I have started my own Substack, so please subscribe to my newsletter if you can.
turns.zh: 我常泡在 LinkedIn，但也开了自己的 Substack，所以如果可以，请订阅我的 newsletter。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Definitely do.
turns.zh: 一定要订。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: I put more short content on LinkedIn and longer form explanations in my Substack, not to compete with your Lenny Newsletter-
turns.zh: 我在 LinkedIn 放更多短内容，在 Substack 放更长篇的解释——不是要跟你 Lenny Newsletter 竞争——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: No, there's-
turns.zh: 不，有——

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... but these are-
turns.zh: ……但这些是——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: ... there's plenty of room for everyone. I recommend yours within Substack and we're going to link to it, and definitely there's like no reason not to subscribe if you're listening to this podcast. It's only upside.
turns.zh: ……地方够所有人用。我推荐你的 Substack，我们会链过去；听这播客的人没理由不订，只有好处。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: Well, thank you. We're also creating PLG course with Reforge that is going to go into very nitty-gritty details of everything that I'm talking about to help you operationalize these concepts. It's launching in fall-
turns.zh: 好，谢谢你。我们也在和 Reforge 做一门 PLG 课程，会把我聊的所有东西抠到极细，帮你把这些概念落地。它秋天——

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh awesome.
turns.zh: 哦太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: Elena Verna
turns.en: ... so do check that out. Other than that, I'm a really big believer in democratizing knowledge so we don't have to all make the same mistakes over and over again, so the biggest way that you can help me is to share your insight, share your knowledge, and share your learnings so we can all grow so much faster together.
turns.zh: ……上线，所以去瞧瞧。除此之外，我极度相信知识民主化，这样我们就不必一遍遍犯同样的错。所以你能帮我最大的方式，就是分享你的洞察、分享你的知识、分享你的学习，这样我们才能一起长得快得多。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Well, you're one of the best at doing that, and thank you again for doing this.
turns.zh: 嗯，你是最擅长做这个的人之一，再次谢谢你。

turns.en: Thank you for having me, Lenny.
turns.zh: 谢谢你邀我，Lenny。
